questions.prompt: What is the main purpose of this fixed fiscal-year report excerpt?
options: To explain how payment timing affects the comparison between two fiscal years.
To present CBO’s forthcoming economic projections for the 2026–2036 period.
To explain why budget committees requested a report during a funding lapse.
To summarize fiscal-year budget changes and explain limits to the comparisons.
answers: To summarize fiscal-year budget changes and explain limits to the comparisons.
questions.explanation:
报告概括2025财年赤字、收入、支出和公共债务变化，并说明付款时间挪移、数据更新及缺失对比较的影响。其他选项各抓住一个局部说明或未来报告，不能代替全文主旨。

选项“To explain how payment timing affects the comparison between two fiscal years.”：付款时间确实影响比较，但只是一个解释段，没有覆盖收入、支出、债务和其他数据限制。
选项“To present CBO’s forthcoming economic projections for the 2026–2036 period.”：文中只是预告未来报告，没有在本节选中展示2026–2036完整预测。
选项“To explain why budget committees requested a report during a funding lapse.”：这是末段的发布背景，不是全文对财年数据变化的主要说明。
选项“To summarize fiscal-year budget changes and explain limits to the comparisons.”：正确：既有年度变动，也有时间、更新数据和数据缺失等解释。
questions.evidence: In fiscal year 2025, which ended on September 30, the federal budget deficit totaled $1.8 trillion—a decrease of $41 billion (or 2 percent) from the shortfall recorded in the previous year. Revenues and outlays alike increased from 2024 totals. Revenues rose by 6 percent, or $317 billion; increases in collections of individual income taxes and customs duties were partially offset by a decline in corporate tax receipts. Outlays grew by 4 percent, or $275 billion, with increases occurring in several areas, including the largest benefit programs and net interest on the public debt (which, for the first time, surpassed $1 trillion). Those increases were partly offset by decreases recorded for federal student loan programs, deposit insurance, and the Small Business Administration. The 2025 amounts reported here differ somewhat from amounts described in the Monthly Budget Review: September 2025 because they reflect the subsequently reported data in the Monthly Treasury Statement for September 2025.

questions.prompt: Why were some outlays shifted from fiscal year 2024 into 2023?
options: The first day of fiscal year 2024 fell on a weekend.
All federal benefit programmes were permanently cancelled.
Corporate tax receipts had increased by exactly $72 billion.
The public debt had already fallen to zero.
answers: The first day of fiscal year 2024 fell on a weekend.
questions.explanation:
原文先说October 1（财年首日）适逢周末，再说因此某些付款提前到前一财年。它是付款时间的变化，不是取消项目或债务归零。

选项“The first day of fiscal year 2024 fell on a weekend.”：正确：As a result把周末日期与付款挪移直接连接。
选项“All federal benefit programmes were permanently cancelled.”：原文没有全部永久取消福利项目。
选项“Corporate tax receipts had increased by exactly $72 billion.”：72 billion是挪移的付款总额，不是公司税收入增长。
选项“The public debt had already fallen to zero.”：原文没有债务归零，反而说明公共债务占经济比重上升。
questions.evidence: Outlays in fiscal year 2024 were reduced because October 1 (the first day of the fiscal year) fell on a weekend. As a result, certain payments totaling $72 billion were shifted from 2024 into 2023. If not for those shifts, the deficit in 2025 would have been 6 percent smaller—instead of 2 percent smaller—than it was in 2024.

questions.prompt: What does “Those increases” refer to in the first paragraph?
options: The rises in individual income tax collections and customs duties.
The increases in the two years’ gross domestic product.
The spending increases in areas including major benefit programmes and debt interest.
The reductions for student loan programmes and deposit insurance.
answers: The spending increases in areas including major benefit programmes and debt interest.
questions.explanation:

选项“The reductions for student loan programmes and deposit insurance.”：reductions/decreases与increases方向相反，是部分抵消增加的项目。

questions.prompt: Choose TRUE, FALSE or NOT GIVEN: The deficit was a smaller percentage of GDP in 2025 than in 2024.
options: TRUE
FALSE
NOT GIVEN
questions.explanation:
原文给2025为5.9%，2024为6.3%；5.9小于6.3。这里比较赤字占GDP比例，不是赤字总额与全部公共债务混为一个指标。

选项“TRUE”：正确：5.9%低于6.3%。
选项“FALSE”：FALSE与所列比例直接相反。
选项“NOT GIVEN”：不是NOT GIVEN，两个年度比例都列出。
questions.evidence: The federal deficit in 2025 was equal to 5.9 percent of the nation’s gross domestic product (GDP), a decrease from 6.3 percent of GDP in 2024. The 2025 deficit expressed as a percentage of GDP is greater than the 50 year average of 3.8 percent and has been exceeded only eight times since 1946 (from 2009 through 2012 and in 2020, 2021, 2023, and 2024). Federal debt held by the public increased in 2025 relative to the size of the economy—rising to 99.8 percent from 97.4 percent of GDP at the end of fiscal year 2024.
distractorReasons: FALSE与所列比例直接相反。
不是NOT GIVEN，两个年度比例都列出。

FALSE
NOT GIVEN
questions.explanation:

grammarEvidence.sentence: Revenues rose by 6 percent, or $317 billion; increases in collections of individual income taxes and customs duties were partially offset by a decline in corporate tax receipts.
grammarEvidence.explanation: rose by说明增长幅度，不是增长后的总额；were partially offset by是被动结构，指一部分增长被公司税收入下降抵消。partially不能改成全部抵消，revenues也不等同某个家庭的税额。

grammarEvidence.sentence: If not for those shifts, the deficit in 2025 would have been 6 percent smaller—instead of 2 percent smaller—than it was in 2024.
grammarEvidence.explanation: If not for...省略形式表达与过去实际情况不同的假设，主句would have been说明若没有那些时间挪移，比较结果会怎样。文中实际同比少2%，6%是这一反事实调整后的比较，不是两个同时发生的实际降幅。
